case_title: Suraj Singh Gujar & Anr. v. The State of Madhya Pradesh & Ors.
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (cousins of the injured respondents 2 and 3; the compromise deed describes the parties as uncle and nephew); prior dispute over land and bullock-tying
statutory_provisions: IPC s.323, s.324, s.325, each read with s.34
evidence_type: Not stated (judgment does not describe trial evidence; the Supreme Court relied on affidavits and the compromise)
mitigating_circumstances: Minor issue underlying the incident; parties are close relatives; disputes settled; unconditional apology tendered; both sides agreed to maintain peace
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under ss.323, 324 and 325 r/w s.34 IPC; rigorous imprisonment of three months, six months and one year respectively
high_court_outcome: Appeal (CRLA No. 1999 of 2013) dismissed on 26.12.2023; conviction and sentence maintained
neutral_facts: On 20 May 2011, a dispute arose between the accused and the victim over a minor matter. The victim was attempting to tie bullocks when the accused objected, asserting that the land belonged to them. The accused and the victim are close relatives. Injuries were caused to persons on the victim's side, but the record does not describe the nature or extent of those injuries. The offences alleged were hurt offences under sections 323, 324 and 325 of the Indian Penal Code, read with section 34. The record does not describe the weapon used, the eyewitnesses, the medical evidence, the investigation, or the statements recorded during the trial. No confession or recovery is mentioned. The available account therefore rests on the nature of the dispute and the charges alone, and the evidence presented at trial cannot be reconstructed from this document.
physical_harm: Injuries to the injured persons on the victim's side; nature and extent not described; no death
premeditation_planning: Not found; the Court described the incident as arising from a minor issue
motive: alleged: objection to the victim tying bullocks, with the accused asserting the land was theirs
key_evidence_accepted: Affidavits of the injured respondents and respondent no. 4 agreeing to compounding; the Court did not rely on trial evidence
post_offence_conduct: Accused tendered an unconditional apology regarding the incident, as noted by the Court
custody_duration: Not stated (the Court noted the appellants are already outside jail)
trial_duration: offence: 20.05.2011; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 26.12.2023; Supreme Court: 30.08.2024
legal_representation: Accused: Ms. Deeksha Saggi, Abhishek Kumar, Rituparn Uniyal, K Anil Singh, Ram Lal Roy (Advs.). State and respondents: D. S. Parmar, A.A.G., Ms. Mrinal Gopal Elker, Abhimanyu Singh-G.a., and others (Advs.)
investigation_status: FIR referred to; charge sheet and investigation steps not described
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.323, 324, 325 r/w s.34 IPC. High Court: appeal dismissed 26.12.2023, conviction and sentence maintained. Supreme Court: leave granted; conviction set aside under Art.142 on 30.08.2024
prosecution_argument: Not stated (State's submissions not recorded; the injured respondents agreed to compounding)
defence_argument: Dispute settled with the injured persons by compromise deed dated 29.01.2024; accused sought permission to compound the offences
legal_principle_applied: Power under Art.142 may be exercised beyond s.320 CrPC in exceptional cases, weighing nature and effect of offence on society, seriousness of injury, voluntariness of compromise, and conduct of accused
precedent_relied_upon: Ramgopal & Anr. v. State of M.P (2022) 14 SCC 531 (relied on); Murali v. State (2021) 1 SCC 726, Manjit Singh v. State of Punjab (2020) 18 SCC 777, Kailash Chand v. State of Rajasthan (2021) 18 SCC 534, Srinivasan Iyenger v. Bimla Devi Agarwal (2019) 4 SCC 456, Ramawatar v. State of M.P (2022) 13 SCC 635 (cited)
sentencing_rationale: Not applicable (no sentence imposed); conviction set aside in view of the compromise between close relatives, the minor nature of the issue, and the agreement to maintain peace
judicial_mitigating_factors: Minor issue; close relatives; disputes settled; unconditional apology; agreement to maintain peace and harmony
other_sentence_order: Appellants, already outside jail, need not surrender; appeal disposed of along with pending applications
